translationRepairs: Born Song Wentong, he served as a soldier in the Boye Army and was posted to Fengxiang.
Originally surnamed Song with the given name Wentong, he served as a soldier in the Boye Army and was posted to Fengxiang.
本姓宋，名文通 explicitly gives the original surname Song and given name Wentong; it is not a birth formula.
Fengxiang lies too close to Chang’an—strike at him and you court disaster you cannot undo. Another day, even if you killed a scapegoat to appease the warlords, you might not be able to.”
Fengxiang lies too close to Chang’an—strike at him and you court disaster you cannot undo. Another day, even if you wished to execute Chao Cuo to appease the feudal lords, you might not be able to.”
晁錯 names the Han statesman Chao Cuo; replacing him with the generic word scapegoat erases the historical allusion.
Maozhen asked that his son Congmi hold Xingyuan in his stead. Zhaozong moved Maozhen to Shannan West and sent Chancellor Xu Yanruo to Fengxiang.
Maozhen asked that his son Jimi hold Xingyuan in his stead. Zhaozong moved Maozhen to Shannan West and sent Chancellor Xu Yanruo to Fengxiang.
繼密 is Jimi; Congmi incorrectly reads 繼 as though it were 從.
The next year Wang Chongying of Hedong died, and his sons Ke and Gong fought over the circuit.
The next year Wang Chongying of Hezhong died, and his sons Ke and Gong fought over the circuit.
河中 is Hezhong, not Hedong, which is written 河東.
The coup failed, and Jin marched as well. Maozhen, afraid, killed Chancellors Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi, left his adopted son Congpeng with two thousand men as palace guard, and withdrew.
The coup failed, and Jin marched as well. Maozhen, afraid, killed Chancellors Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi, left his adopted son Jipeng with two thousand men as palace guard, and withdrew.
繼鵬 is Jipeng; Congpeng incorrectly reads 繼 as though it were 從.
Jin reached Hedong. Congpeng and Xingyu’s brother Xingshi fought to drag Zhaozong away. Chang’an convulsed. The emperor took refuge at Shimen.
Jin reached Hezhong. Jipeng and Xingyu’s brother Xingshi fought to drag Zhaozong away. Chang’an convulsed. The emperor took refuge at Shimen.
河中 is Hezhong and 繼鵬 is Jipeng; both forms in the original translation are erroneous.
Maozhen marched to E County and killed Congpeng to buy his peace.
Maozhen marched to E County and killed Jipeng to buy his peace.
繼鵬 is Jipeng; Congpeng incorrectly reads 繼 as though it were 從.
Chief Eunuch Han Quanhui and his faction leaned on Maozhen’s power. Maozhen sent his son Congyun with thousands of men into the capital. Backed by Qi’s army, the eunuchs grew brazen and ungovernable.
Chief Eunuch Han Quanhui and his faction leaned on Maozhen’s power. Maozhen sent his son Jiyun with thousands of men into the capital. Backed by Qi’s army, the eunuchs grew brazen and ungovernable.
繼筠 is Jiyun; Congyun incorrectly reads 繼 as though it were 從.
In Tianfu 1 (901) Yin called Zhu Wen west. Liang reached Tongzhou. Quanhui and his party, terrified, joined Congyun and dragged Zhaozong to Fengxiang.
In Tianfu 1 (901) Yin called Zhu Wen west. Liang reached Tongzhou. Quanhui and his party, terrified, joined Jiyun and dragged Zhaozong to Fengxiang.
繼筠 is Jiyun; Congyun incorrectly reads 繼 as though it were 從.
Cheng Ji of Jingnan then falsely took the surname Guo and was likewise skilled at pacifying Jing-Chu.
Cheng Rui of Jingnan then falsely took the surname Guo and was likewise skilled at pacifying Jing-Chu.
成汭 is Cheng Rui; Ji is not a reading of the given name 汭.
When Wang Chongying of Hedong died, his sons Ke and Gong fought over the circuit. Jin backed Ke; Jian, Wang Xingyu, and Li Maozhen backed Gong.
When Wang Chongying of Hezhong died, his sons Ke and Gong fought over the circuit. Jin backed Ke; Jian, Wang Xingyu, and Li Maozhen backed Gong.
河中 is Hezhong, not Hedong, which is written 河東.
During Zhu Mei’s revolt, Sijing and Li Sixiao of Bin encamped at Wei Bridge.
During Zhu Mei’s revolt, Sijing and Li Sixiao of Fu Prefecture encamped at Wei Bridge.
鄜州 is Fu Prefecture, not Binzhou, which is written 邠州.
Yang Chongben grew up in Li Maozhen’s service, was adopted, took the Li surname and the name Jihui, and was made commissioner of Jingnan.
Yang Chongben grew up in Li Maozhen's service, was adopted, took the Li surname and the name Jihui, and was made military commissioner of the Jingnan Army circuit.
靜難軍 is the Jingnan Army circuit, distinct from the Jingnan region 荊南; identifying it as an Army circuit is clear without a literal parenthetical gloss.
Li Yanrong of Bin and Li Yanyu of Fang abandoned their posts and ran.
Li Yanrong of Fu Prefecture and Li Yanyu of Fang abandoned their posts and ran.
鄜州 is Fu Prefecture, not Binzhou, which is written 邠州.
Another son, Yunquan, was magistrate of Fushi under Later Jin’s Kaiyun era, then retired home.
Wanjin’s son Yunquan was magistrate of Fushi under Later Jin’s Kaiyun era, then retired home.
萬金子允權 means Wanjin's son Yunquan; it does not continue the children of Wanxing from the preceding passage.
Wanxing’s son Yunquan, in the Kaiyun era, was magistrate of Fushi; removed, he lived at home.
Wanjin’s son Yunquan, in the Kaiyun era, was magistrate of Fushi; removed, he lived at home.
萬金子允權 means Wanjin's son Yunquan, not Wanxing's son.

Tao was in his post seven years; of the Tang imperial tombs within his territory he opened them all, took the gold and treasure stored there—and of them Zhaoling was the most secure; Tao went down the spirit passage, saw the palace halls grand and bright, no different from the human world; in the center was the main chamber, east and west wings lined with stone couches; on the couches stone caskets held iron cases, all storing books and maps of former ages, clocks and Wang Xizhi’s traces; paper and ink were as new; Tao took them all, and they passed into the world—only Qianling, in wind and rain, could not be opened.

Tao was in his post seven years; of the Tang imperial tombs within his territory he opened them all, took the gold and treasure stored there—and of them Zhaoling was the most secure; Tao went down the spirit passage, saw the palace halls grand and bright, no different from the human world; in the center was the main chamber, east and west wings lined with stone couches; on the couches stone caskets held iron cases, all storing books and maps of former ages, Zhong Yao’s and Wang Xizhi’s calligraphy traces; paper and ink were as new; Tao took them all, and they passed into the world—only Qianling, in wind and rain, could not be opened.
鐘、王筆跡 abbreviates the calligraphy of Zhong Yao and Wang Xizhi; 鐘 is not a reference to clocks here.
When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Tao came from Xu to court, bribed Empress Liu through the actor Jing Jin, and won her word. Zhuangzong favored him lavishly and renamed him Li Shaogong.
When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Tao came from Xu to court, bribed Empress Liu through the actor Jing Jin, and won her word. Zhuangzong favored him lavishly and renamed him Li Shaochong.
The bestowed name 李紹沖 is Li Shaochong; Shaogong misreads the final character 沖.
